Space is the vast region beyond Earth's atmosphere.
It contains stars, planets, and galaxies.

Outer space is mostly empty but filled with radiation.
It extends infinitely across the universe.

Gravity is a force that pulls objects with mass toward each other.
It keeps planets orbiting the Sun.

Gravity acts between all objects with mass.
Stronger mass means stronger pull.

There are 8 planets in our solar system.
They orbit the Sun in fixed paths.
The planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

Earth is the only known planet with life.
It has water, oxygen, and suitable conditions.

Earth’s atmosphere protects life.
It also maintains stable temperatures.

The Sun is a star at the center of our solar system.
It provides energy for life.

It produces energy through nuclear fusion.
This powers Earth’s climate and ecosystems.

The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.
It reflects sunlight, making it visible.

It affects ocean tides.
It has no atmosphere and a rocky surface.

Mars is called the Red Planet due to iron oxide.
It has a thin atmosphere.

Scientists study Mars for future colonization.
Conditions are harsh but promising.

A black hole has extremely strong gravity.
Nothing, not even light, can escape it.

They form when massive stars collapse.
They warp space and time.

Stars are massive balls of gas.
They produce energy through nuclear fusion.

They shine due to fusion reactions.
This releases enormous energy.

patterns: Which galaxy do we live in
responses:
A galaxy is a system of stars and planets.
We live in the Milky Way.

The Milky Way has billions of stars.
Our solar system is a small part of it.

Rockets work by expelling gas downward.
This creates thrust upward.

They follow Newton’s third law.
Every action has an equal reaction.

Astronauts travel and work in space.
They conduct experiments and missions.

They undergo rigorous training.
They operate spacecraft and research equipment.

A light-year is a unit of distance.
It is how far light travels in a year.

It helps measure huge space distances.
Light travels about 9.46 trillion km yearly.

Satellites orbit planets.
They can be natural or artificial.

Artificial satellites help in communication.
They also provide GPS and weather data.

The ISS is a space station orbiting Earth.
Astronauts live and work there.

It is used for scientific research.
It is a collaboration of multiple countries.

Exoplanets are planets outside our solar system.
They orbit other stars.

Thousands have been discovered.
Some may support life.

Dark matter is invisible and does not emit light.
It makes up most of the universe's mass.

It is detected through gravity.
Its nature is still unknown.

There is no confirmed evidence of aliens.
Scientists continue searching.

Life beyond Earth is possible.
But not proven yet.
